html:
SMTO-GML-0055 — The email or draft changed since SMTO selected it

GUID: e44a4301-3583-5940-9a6c-ed276c752b0f
Slug: gmail-imap-identity-changed
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail_imap

What happened

  • SMTO went back to the email or draft it had picked, but it had been edited, sent, deleted, or could no longer be told apart from another item. SMTO stopped so it wouldn't act on the wrong mail.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail and find the draft or email. Check whether it was edited, sent, or deleted after you asked SMTO to work on it. SMTO refuses to replace or tidy up a draft that was changed or sent in the meantime.
  2. If the email already appears in Sent, keep it and don't ask SMTO to send it again. Sending it again would deliver a duplicate to your recipients.
  3. Ask SMTO to find the email or draft again so it uses the current version, then ask only for the part that hasn't happened yet. A fresh lookup gives SMTO the item as it exists now, so the check passes.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the current email or draft, and the action completes once with no duplicate in Gmail.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend an email just to clear an old draft; delete a leftover draft yourself in Gmail if you need to.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Revalidation of the selected Gmail message or draft by X-GM-MSGID failed: no match or multiple matches, a mismatched message ID, a draft that lost \Draft or gained \Sent, or a draft whose content fingerprint changed.

What this means

  • The selected message or draft could not be revalidated against its current Gmail identity and state. Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.

Why this can happen

  • Producer condition: The selected message or draft could not be revalidated against its current Gmail identity and state.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact account revision, Gateway route and failing substep with the retained receipt.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the message or draft (get_message or get_draft) to obtain its current ID and state, and compare it with the earlier reference. Keep any confirmed send or replacement draft recorded in the receipt, and never resend mail just to complete draft cleanup.
  • Read the current message or draft again and review its exact reference. Preserve any confirmed send or replacement draft; never resend just to repair cleanup.

Retry and execution caution

  • Preserve confirmed work and establish the current mailbox state before any repeated write.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen operation completes with a matching receipt, or the remaining uncertain action is inspected in Gmail without duplicate mail.

What not to do

  • Do not switch accounts or authentication methods after failure, or automatically replay uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.
  • App-password setup: https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
